title: Fact provenance is multi-fragment but single-source-assertion scoped
failure_signature: FactAssertion collapses back to one evidence_fragment_id, loses evidence roles during persistence/reload, or combines fragments from different source documents into one assertion and thereby blurs source quality/known-time lineage.
root_cause: The domain model lagged behind the existing assertion_evidence many-to-many table, while Judgment already modeled explicit evidence refs. A single-fragment field made provenance asymmetric and tempted callers to treat corroboration across sources as one claim.
invariant: FactAssertion owns one or more typed FactEvidenceRef values, including at least one supporting fragment. Roles survive persistence/reload. All fragments on one FactAssertion belong to that assertion's extraction document; independent-source corroboration remains separate assertions so source and known-time semantics stay attributable.
anti_regression: Do not reintroduce evidence_fragment_id as the FactAssertion domain/output contract; the current legacy input bridge is migration-only and may be removed.
Do not flatten evidence roles when loading assertions from PostgreSQL.
Do not merge evidence from multiple source documents into one FactAssertion to simulate corroboration.

guards.contains: FactAssertion requires at least one supporting evidence fragment
guards.description: Domain validation requires non-empty unique evidence refs with a supporting role.
Database constrains the same explicit Fact evidence roles.

guards.contains: FactAssertion evidence must exist on its extraction document
guards.description: PostgreSQL write path rejects fragments outside the assertion extraction document.

revisit_when: Revisit only if provenance is replaced by a richer claim graph that preserves fragment roles, source/document attribution and known-time independently; a convenience single-evidence API is not sufficient.
